description: Make cam run the single hub: CLI subcommands become thin-proxies that push natural-language requests to the orchestrator pane via tmux send-keys, and all worker dispatch flows through a single reused titled worker-pane that reports on /exit (push) instead of being polled (pull).

officialDocsConsulted.summary: send-keys -l sends literal UTF-8 and disables key-name lookup; arbitrary text (JSON braces/quotes/semicolons) is otherwise parsed as key names; Enter is a distinct key from literal text; set -p @user-option + pane-border-format #{@option} for the titled pill. Per-pane user options are set with the set -p form (e.g. tmux set -p @cam_label <value>), not set -g.

userStories.title: Uniform titled worker-pane (single reused pane, label per phase)
userStories.description: As the orchestrator, I need worker dispatches to reuse ONE titled worker-pane (not spawn a fresh pane per dispatch) so that the tmux session has 2 panes at rest and 3 panes when a worker is active. The pane's pane-border-format pulls the green pill already used by the orchestrator/dashboard, and the worker process runs claude --agent X WITHOUT the orchestrator's kill-session wrapper so that /exit closes only the pane (session survives).
acceptanceCriteria: A worker dispatch sets @cam_label per phase and reuses the existing worker-pane if one is present (no second worker-pane spawned).
The worker-pane pane-border-format renders the same green pill (pane-border-status top / pane-border-format #{@cam_label}) the orchestrator and dashboard already use.
The worker argv does NOT wrap claude in a kill-session shell wrapper; /exit closes only the worker-pane and the tmux session keeps running.
claude -p is not present in the worker argv (CAM-42 rule; existing test asserts this).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files likely touched: src/commands/run.ts, src/tmux/session.ts (look for the pane-spawn helper and the existing pane-border-format wiring for the orchestrator/dashboard). Patterns.md invariants to re-check: Bun runtime (Bun.spawn for tmux calls or Bun.$ via runTmux helper); never reintroduce claude -p in a worker argv (test/no-claude-p-in-worker.* asserts this); never register a --permission-mode flag on a subcommand; noUncheckedIndexedAccess (guard array/regex captures); Ink screens are not changed by this story, but if you touch any divider, success/failure is the glyph not the divider color. userStories.title: isSessionStale + orchestrator-alive + pane-count mutex predicate
userStories.description: As the dispatch layer, I need isSessionStale (src/tmux/session.ts:136) to treat 2 OR 3 panes as alive (the 3rd being the titled worker-pane, not a stray cat/process), an orchestrator-alive predicate, and a pane-count mutex predicate (a dispatch may spawn the 3rd pane only if exactly 2 panes currently exist). This closes the CAM-47 false-positive where a stale-check killed a session with a legitimate worker-pane.
acceptanceCriteria: isSessionStale returns 'alive' for both 2-pane and 3-pane states where the 3rd pane is the titled worker-pane (identifiable by @cam_label), and returns 'stale' for stray panes (cat, leftover shell) as before.
An orchestrator-alive predicate exists (e.g. is %0 the orchestrator pane and is it running the orchestrator process) and is exported for thin-proxies to call.
A pane-count mutex predicate exists: returns 'available' iff exactly 2 panes currently exist, 'busy' otherwise. Thin-proxies use this to decide whether to dispatch a 3rd pane.
Unit tests cover the 2-pane / 3-pane / stray-pane / dead-orchestrator cases via an injected runTmux fake.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files likely touched: src/tmux/session.ts (isSessionStale lives at line 136). userStories.title: cam plan / next / issue thin-proxies + .claude/.cam-orch-ready bootstrap-wait
userStories.description: As an operator, I need cam plan, cam next, and cam issue to become thin-proxies: if a live orchestrator is detected, atomic send-keys a natural-language request into %0 and return (fire-and-forget); if not, bootstrap cam run, poll the .claude/.cam-orch-ready marker until ready, then send-keys. The orchestrator writes the marker after its own boot completes.
acceptanceCriteria: cam plan, cam next, cam issue detect a live orchestrator (via the US-005 predicate); on hit they send-keys a natural-language request to %0 (atomic text+Enter, -l for literal payloads) and return.
On miss they bootstrap cam run, then poll for .claude/.cam-orch-ready (a fresh marker written by the orchestrator after boot) before pushing send-keys.
cam run writes .claude/.cam-orch-ready after orchestrator boot completes; the marker is cleared on orchestrator exit.
A bootstrap-wait helper exists (mirror the existing setup.ts sentinel-poll pattern) and is unit-tested with an injected file-stat fake.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files likely touched: src/commands/plan.ts, src/commands/next.ts, src/commands/issue.ts, src/commands/run.ts (marker write/clear), plus a new bootstrap-wait helper (e.g. src/tmux/bootstrap-wait.ts). Mirror the existing setup.ts sentinel-poll for the marker polling. Patterns.md invariants to re-check: send-keys atomic text+Enter; -l for literal payloads; Bun.file for the marker; never register a --permission-mode flag on these subcommands (CAM-42 + test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts); noUncheckedIndexedAccess; no claude -p in any spawned worker argv; conventional commits. The .claude/.cam-orch-ready marker cleanup must be wired into an exit/finally handler in src/commands/run.ts that also fires on SIGINT/SIGTERM (a crash otherwise leaves a stale marker); the thin-proxy bootstrap-wait must additionally re-validate liveness via the US-005 orchestrator-alive predicate before trusting the marker.

userStories.title: Idle-guarantee before pushing into the orchestrator pane
userStories.description: As a thin-proxy or worker, I need to verify the orchestrator pane is idle and ready-for-input before send-keys, so that a pushed request or report never lands mid-turn. The check polls captured pane content until the prompt is stable (no progress glyph, no in-flight tool call) and only then issues send-keys.

The idle-check has a documented timeout and a defined fallback (e.g. log + still send, or block and surface a clear UX) so it never hangs indefinitely.
Unit tests cover the idle / busy / timeout cases via an injected capture-pane fake.

userStories.title: Mutex failure-mode UX when a 2nd dispatch is attempted with a worker active

acceptanceCriteria: When the pane-count mutex predicate (US-005) returns 'busy', the dispatch sites refuse to spawn and surface a clear, single-line message: 'worker busy, blocked until the worker-pane closes' (or operator-approved wording).
A defined exit/queue behavior: thin-proxies exit with a non-zero status, the orchestrator declines and narrates the block; no 4th pane is ever spawned.
Unit tests assert the 'busy' path returns the documented exit/queue behavior on every dispatch site.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
